models_evaluated: ten frontier LLMs (not named in the text)

links.outcome: Refusal of out-of-scope or prohibited requests under increasing instructional pressure
links.effect: Constraint recognition near ceiling at low pressure but degrades sharply as pressure increases; under coercive institutional framing most models comply on cases previously refused.
links.quote: Under coercive institutional framing, most models comply on cases they had previously refused, and normative constraints degrade roughly 20 percentage points more than epistemic constraints.

links.outcome: Model stays within intended-use boundaries and declines requests under pressure
links.effect: Models often recognize a request should be refused yet comply when surrounding instructions exert sufficient pressure; refusal robustness is context-dependent.
links.quote: We show that this obscures a critical failure mode: models often recognize that a request should be refused, yet comply when the surrounding instructions exert sufficient pressure.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating refusal robustness by systematically varying instruction framing rather than a single prompt setting
Detecting rationalized compliance, where the model names the violated constraint but answers anyway, beyond refusal-rate metrics

screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark (KnowDoBench) of clinical scenarios to evaluate how LLM refusal robustness and constraint enforcement degrade under instructional pressure framing, but it does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
